steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Different types of line serve different purposes: contour lines define edges, gestural lines capture movement, analytical lines record accurate proportions.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Mark-making is the foundation of drawing — experiment with pressure, speed, direction and media to create varied marks.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Hatching and cross-hatching build tone through overlapping lines; stippling uses dots; both can describe form and texture.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Expressive line can convey emotion and energy; analytical line prioritises accuracy and measurement.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Create a series of experimental studies exploring mark making and line. Annotate your process. | Research an artist or designer who works with mark making and line. Write a critical analysis of their approach and explain how it has informed your own work. | Evaluate the effectiveness of your experiments with mark making and line. Which approaches were most successful and why?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A range of experimental studies showing different approaches to mark making and line, each annotated with media, technique and purpose. Show development from initial experiments to refined outcomes. | A critical analysis naming a specific artist/designer, using specialist vocabulary, explaining their context and approach, and making clear connections to personal work. | A reflective evaluation identifying successful and less successful experiments, explaining WHY using technical and conceptual language, and showing how evaluation led to further refinement.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Address ALL four Assessment Objectives — AO1 (develop), AO2 (refine), AO3 (record), AO4 (present) Show the FULL creative journey — from initial research to final outcome Annotate your work using specialist vocabulary (not just "I like it") Draw from primary sources wherever possible — real objects, not photos Experiment with a RANGE of media and techniques before selecting Make clear connections between artist research and your own developing work
